images.title: A Roman product is not a landmark
images.purpose: Shows that V × L is 250, which needs several symbols, CCL, instead of a single landmark.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Two symbol cards with a times sign on the left, an equals sign, and three tiles on the right.
images.exact_structure: Left: one tile V and one tile L, white with dark outlines, with a × sign between them. Then an equals sign. Right: three tiles C, C, L in a row, together outlined by one vermilion (#D55E00) rounded box labelled not one symbol. Under the whole line, in grey (#6B7280): 5 × 50 = 250. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Multiplying two Roman landmarks often gives a number with no single symbol, so there is no simple rule.
images.description: Shows that V × L is 250, which needs several symbols, CCL, instead of a single landmark.
images.context: Other products in the example: L × D = 25000 (25 M's), V × D = MMD, VII × IX = LXIII.

image_decisions.why: The difficulty of Roman multiplication shows best as one product spilling into several symbols.
